name.text: Same direction opposite or not parallel

questiontext.text:
\(\mathbf{a} = {@col(av)@}\). For each vector, choose whether it is a multiple of \(\mathbf{a}\) in the same direction, a multiple in the opposite direction, or not parallel to \(\mathbf{a}\).

(a) \({@col(w1)@}\): [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
(b) \({@col(w2)@}\): [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]
(c) \({@col(w3)@}\): [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]
(d) \({@col(w4)@}\): [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
A vector is parallel to \(\mathbf{a}\) when it is a multiple \(k\mathbf{a}\): divide each component by the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\). If you get the same number k both times, it is \(k\mathbf{a}\); k positive means the same direction, k negative the opposite direction.

  • (a) [[if test="is(cat1<3)"]]Each component is \({@kv1@}\) times the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\). \({@kv1@}\) is [[if test="is(kv1<0)"]]negative, so the direction is opposite.[[else]]positive, so the direction is the same.[[/if]][[else]]Divide each component by the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\): you get \({@r11@}\) and \({@r12@}\). They are not equal, so this vector is not a multiple of \(\mathbf{a}\).[[/if]]
  • (b) [[if test="is(cat2<3)"]]Each component is \({@kv2@}\) times the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\). \({@kv2@}\) is [[if test="is(kv2<0)"]]negative, so the direction is opposite.[[else]]positive, so the direction is the same.[[/if]][[else]]Divide each component by the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\): you get \({@r21@}\) and \({@r22@}\). They are not equal, so this vector is not a multiple of \(\mathbf{a}\).[[/if]]
  • (c) [[if test="is(cat3<3)"]]Each component is \({@kv3@}\) times the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\). \({@kv3@}\) is [[if test="is(kv3<0)"]]negative, so the direction is opposite.[[else]]positive, so the direction is the same.[[/if]][[else]]Divide each component by the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\): you get \({@r31@}\) and \({@r32@}\). They are not equal, so this vector is not a multiple of \(\mathbf{a}\).[[/if]]
  • (d) [[if test="is(cat4<3)"]]Each component is \({@kv4@}\) times the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\). \({@kv4@}\) is [[if test="is(kv4<0)"]]negative, so the direction is opposite.[[else]]positive, so the direction is the same.[[/if]][[else]]Divide each component by the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\): you get \({@r41@}\) and \({@r42@}\). They are not equal, so this vector is not a multiple of \(\mathbf{a}\).[[/if]]

questiondescription.text:
Vectors: parallel vectors and scalar multiples

Grade 12 CBE Essential 2.2: Decide whether each of four column vectors is a multiple of a in the same direction, in the opposite direction, or not parallel to a.

Essential

This question is adapted from Question B1 in Section B and Question 5 in Exercise B of Chapter 9 of Instone, S., Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP AS/A2 Mathematics: Core 4 for AQA, Cambridge University Press, 2005: new numbers, Kenyan context, STACK randomisation, three categories with the direction asked, with named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: [[if test="is(cat1<3)"]][[if test="is(cat1=1)"]]You chose the opposite direction. A multiple of \(\mathbf{a}\) in the opposite direction is a negative number times \(\mathbf{a}\), so both its components have the opposite signs to those of \(\mathbf{a}\), as in \(-\mathbf{a} = {@col(-av)@}\). Compare the signs in this vector with the signs in \(\mathbf{a}\).[[else]]You chose the same direction. A multiple of \(\mathbf{a}\) in the same direction is a positive number times \(\mathbf{a}\), so both its components keep the signs of those of \(\mathbf{a}\), as in \(2\mathbf{a} = {@col(2*av)@}\). Compare the signs in this vector with the signs in \(\mathbf{a}\).[[/if]][[else]]You chose the same direction, so this vector would be \(k\mathbf{a}\) for one positive number k. Test it: the top numbers give \(k = {@w1[1]@} \div ({@av[1]@}) = {@r11@}\). Does \({@r11@} \times ({@av[2]@})\) give the bottom number, \({@w1[2]@}\)?[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="is(cat1<3)"]]You chose not parallel. Test it: divide each component by the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\), \({@w1[1]@} \div ({@av[1]@})\) and \({@w1[2]@} \div ({@av[2]@})\). A vector is not parallel only when the two results are different. Work both out.[[else]]You chose the opposite direction, so this vector would be \(k\mathbf{a}\) for one negative number k. Test it: the top numbers give \(k = {@w1[1]@} \div ({@av[1]@}) = {@r11@}\). Does \({@r11@} \times ({@av[2]@})\) give the bottom number, \({@w1[2]@}\)?[[/if]]
